BREAKING:  Weather Update
Typhoon Uwan is expected to cause widespread heavy rains and strong winds across the Philippines, impacting regions from Northern Luzon (Region I) to Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Southern Luzon , Bicol Region, as well as Western, Eastern, and Central Visayas ( Cebu ) , and the Caraga Region in Mindanao, posing serious risks of flooding, landslides, and storm surges throughout the affected areas.

data.raw_text:
#UwanPH (Fung-Wong) strengthened fast tonight just east of the Philippines.

As of tonight, the storm hasn’t been officially declared a super typhoon yet — but based on Dvorak analysis and microwave satellite imagery, it’s already behaving like one. The satellite shows that inner eye wall tightening rapidly, and intensity estimates are now up to 140 knots (around 250 km/h) — right on par with Typhoon Pepito at its peak last year.

👉 Signal Force 4 is now in effect, and I fully expect these warnings to expand along the east coast overnight. A slight southward wobble in the track now brings the center closer to Catanduanes and Aurora Province — and this remains a very large, dangerous storm.

Remember: this isn’t just about the core winds.
🌧️ Heavy rain will bring flooding and landslides — some areas could see 200–300 mm, with runoff into the Cagayan Valley and river rises that may peak after landfall.
🌊 Storm surge of 2–3 meters is possible along the east coast and up to 1–2 meters along Pangasinan and Manila Bay as winds wrap around from the west.
💨 Even Metro Manila could see tropical-storm-force gusts late Sunday into Monday.

Timing:
🕗 Landfall expected Sunday evening in Aurora.
🕓 Impacts already being felt across Catanduanes and Northern Samar.
🕕 Surge and flooding threats continue through Monday morning, especially in low-lying and coastal areas.

This is a powerful, wide-reaching system — so please don’t focus only on the eye or center track. Impacts will stretch far beyond it.
Check PAGASA for official warnings, listen to your local DRRM offices, and make your final preparations tonight.

Stay safe, everyone.

- Robert Speta
#UwanPH #typhoon #Philippines
